ranked.title: Environmental dependence of the properties of H$\alpha$ emitters in the extremely massive galaxy protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 at $z = 2.24$
ranked.abstract: Protoclusters, the progenitors of galaxy clusters, provide ideal laboratories for studying how high-density environments influence galaxy formation and evolution at early cosmic epochs. It remains unclear whether environmental effects on galaxy properties over scales of $>30$ cMpc are already in place at $z > 2$ and how these effects depend on the evolutionary stage of large-scale structures. We investigate the physical properties of H$\alpha$ emitters (HAEs) in two extremely overdense protoclusters, BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, at $z = 2.24$, and explore the environmental dependence of galaxy properties at this redshift. In BOSS1244, we find a clear color-density and stellar mass-density relation. HAEs in higher-density regions are significantly redder in $z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}$ and more massive than those in lower-density regions. In contrast, BOSS1542 shows weak or no such correlations. Red HAEs $(z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}>2.5)$ in both fields are preferentially located in the densest cores, have high stellar masses $(>10^{11}\,M_{\odot})$, high SFRs, and are $4-7$ times more abundant than in general fields. The irregular morphologies observed in some red HAEs are consistent with ongoing mass assembly and may be associated with dust-obscured star formation or galaxy interactions. Both protoclusters broadly follow the star-forming main sequence, but BOSS1542 exhibits a steeper slope, indicating more active star formation in massive galaxies. Our results demonstrate that environmental effects on galaxy properties operate over scales of $\sim39$\,cMpc at $z=2.24$, but their manifestation is strongly dependent on the evolutionary state of the large-scale structure. BOSS1244 appears more evolved, with ongoing galaxy merging and possible quenching, while BOSS1542 remains in an early, filamentary, gas-rich phase.
ranked.reason: Environmental dependence of Halpha emitter properties (mass, SFR, color) in protoclusters — directly touches galaxy evolution/quenching via spectroscopic SFR tracers.

ranked.title: Discovery of Two Hyperluminous Infrared Galaxies at $z\sim6$
ranked.abstract: Hyperluminous infrared galaxies (HyLIRGs) at cosmic dawn are key to understanding the formation of the first massive galaxies. We report the spectroscopic confirmation of two unlensed HyLIRGs at $z\sim6$ in the COSMOS field, AzTECC63 and S2COS-84, originally selected from single-dish AzTEC and SCUBA-2 surveys. Using ALMA and NOEMA observations, we robustly detected CO and [CII] lines in both galaxies and unambiguously confirmed their redshifts to be $z=6.092$ and $z=5.90$, respectively. Panchromatic SED fitting reveals dust-obscured star formation rates of $\approx1000$ and $\approx2300\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, ranking them among the most intensely star-forming systems known at $z \gtrsim 6$. High-resolution ALMA observations reveal an extremely compact morphology for S2COS-84, with a dust-continuum effective radius of $\approx0.3$ kpc, implying a star-formation rate surface density above the Eddington limit. The far-infrared SEDs of both galaxies, together with the compact size of S2COS-84, indicate warm dust ($T_{\rm dust} \approx 80$ K) that is likely optically thick at far-infrared wavelengths. Both galaxies exhibit an extreme [CII] deficit, with $L_{\rm [C\,II]}/L_{\rm IR} \approx 10^{-3.7}$, an order of magnitude below that of normal star-forming galaxies. Their molecular gas masses, derived consistently from both [C\,{\sc ii}] and dust, together with their IR-derived SFRs imply short gas depletion times of $\approx$40--60 Myr, making them plausible progenitors of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies found at $z\sim5$.
ranked.reason: High-z hyperluminous galaxy spectroscopic confirmation with SED/SFR properties, touches galaxy evolution but via dust/CO not stellar population synthesis.

ranked.title: JAISP: A Joint Rubin-Euclid Foundation Model for Cross-Instrument Source Detection and Astrometry
ranked.abstract: Joint pixel-level processing of Rubin and Euclid imaging promises deeper source detection and the cross-survey consistency that precision cosmology requires. We introduce JAISP (Joint AI Survey Processing), a foundation model that learns a single representation of ten-band imaging: Rubin ugrizy and Euclid VIS, Y, J, and H, from the first public releases over $\approx 0.2$ deg$^2$ of the ECDFS deep field. Trained without labels by predicting each band from the other nine, its frozen encoder drives small task-specific networks for source detection and astrometry. The detection network recovers nearly all VIS-selected Euclid Q1 catalog sources on held-out sky, and source injection shows that combining all ten bands extends the point-source detection limit by $\approx 0.3$ mag beyond VIS alone. The astrometry network transfers the sharp VIS localization to the other nine bands, reducing median cross-band positional offsets from $\approx 50$ to $6$--$10$ mas while retaining the full precision of its VIS centroid anchor even for faint sources. Separating this per-source scatter exposes the cross-survey concordance field: a coherent $9$--$10$ mas offset between the two independently Gaia-registered astrometric solutions, dominated by a component common to all bands. Applied without retraining to a second Euclid Deep Field, both networks perform without measurable loss. These gains serve the joint-survey science case: a deeper census recovers faint neighbors whose blending biases weak-lensing shapes and photometric redshifts, and VIS-grade positions in every band supply the common astrometric reference that joint photometry and faint-source proper motions require. A single representation learned once from survey pixels thus serves several measurements across the sky.
ranked.reason: Foundation model for joint Rubin-Euclid imaging source detection — ML/representation-learning methodology relevant as a transferable technique, though applied to imaging not spectra.

ranked.title: Deep UV Spectroscopy of an Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxy at z = 5.725
ranked.abstract: We present deep X-shooter follow-up spectroscopy of AMORE6, an exceptionally metal-poor galaxy at z = 5.725. The new spectrum provides stringent upper limits on rest-frame ultraviolet metal lines, including NV, CIV, NIV], NIII], and OIII]. The non-detection of CIV breaks the density-metallicity degeneracy present in previous analyses based on the [OIII]/Hbeta ratio, excluding the high-density, chemically enriched gas scenario and strengthening the evidence for an extremely metal-poor environment. The X-shooter spectrum also reveals a narrow Lyman-alpha line with a velocity dispersion sigma_v = 23.2 +/- 0.5 km/s and a nearly symmetric profile centered at the systemic redshift measured from Hbeta. Combining the Lyman-alpha line width with the measured source size, we infer a dynamical mass M_dyn = (1-22) x 10^7 Msun, assuming that the line width traces gravitational motions. Spectral energy distribution modeling using Pop III and Pop II stellar population libraries yields stellar masses (1-5) x 10^5 Msun. Although all models reproduce the observed blue UV continuum and Halpha equivalent width (EW), none simultaneously reproduces the Hbeta luminosity and EW, with the observed Hbeta luminosity exceeding the model predictions by up to 3.7 sigma. Possible explanations include departures from standard recombination conditions or limitations in the adopted stellar population models. We discuss possible interpretations of AMORE6, including massive-star formation in an atomic-cooling halo and a gravitationally bound star cluster.
ranked.reason: Deep UV spectroscopy of an extremely metal-poor high-z galaxy with SED/stellar population modeling, moderately aligned with spectroscopy and population inference interests.
ranked.summary: This paper asks whether AMORE6, a galaxy at z=5.725, is truly extremely metal-poor or could instead be dense, chemically enriched gas mimicking that signature. Deep X-shooter spectroscopy rules out the enriched-gas scenario via non-detection of CIV, and a narrow symmetric Lyman-alpha line ($\sigma_v = 23.2$ km/s) combined with source size yields a dynamical mass of $(1-22)\times10^7\,M_\odot$, while SED fitting with Pop III/Pop II libraries gives stellar masses of $(1-5)\times10^5\,M_\odot$. No model simultaneously reproduces the observed H$\beta$ luminosity and equivalent width, with observations exceeding predictions by up to 3.7$\sigma$.
ranked.why: A clear case where standard stellar population/recombination templates fail to fit an extreme, metal-poor object, relevant to anyone pushing full-spectrum fitting methods to their physical limits.

ranked.title: On the effect of a redshift- and metallicity-dependent top-heavy IMF on high-redshift UV luminosity functions
ranked.abstract: JWST observations have revealed a higher-than-expected abundance of bright galaxies at $z \gtrsim 10$. Several scenarios have been proposed to explain this excess, one of which invokes a top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) in the early Universe. In this work, we construct spectral energy distribution (SED) templates based on a redshift- and metallicity-dependent IMF ($z$-$Z$ dependent IMF) motivated by the star-cluster simulations of Chon et al. (2022) and the redshift-dependent IMF model of Steinhardt et al. (2020). We implement these templates in a semi-analytic galaxy model built on a large-box $N$-body simulation to investigate the impact of a top-heavy IMF on the ultraviolet luminosity function (UVLF) of high-redshift galaxies. The adopted $z$-$Z$ dependent IMF enhances the UV luminosity of young stellar populations, particularly at low metallicity, and increases the scatter in the UV luminosity-to-star formation rate conversion factor relative to the Kroupa IMF. Without dust attenuation, both top-heavy IMF models predict a substantially enhanced bright end of the UVLF. However, when dust attenuation is included and calibrated at $z=7$, IMF-dependent metal enrichment and the resulting dust attenuation partly offset the intrinsic UV enhancement. The self-consistent model broadly reproduces the observed UVLF at $z\sim10$, although discrepancies remain at $z\gtrsim12$. For the selected high-redshift UVLF constraints, the best-fitting dust optical depths are 51% and 21% of the fiducial values at $z=9.7$ and $13.04$, respectively, indicating a preference for weaker effective dust attenuation. The highest-redshift comparison does not provide a robust constraint. Our results highlight the importance of accounting for both enhanced stellar UV emission and IMF-dependent metal enrichment and dust attenuation when assessing the impact of a top-heavy IMF on high-redshift galaxies.
ranked.reason: Top-heavy IMF effects on high-z UV luminosity functions via SED modeling, adjacent to stellar population synthesis but focused on cosmic reionization-era photometry not spectroscopy.
ranked.summary: The authors ask whether a redshift- and metallicity-dependent top-heavy IMF can explain the excess of bright galaxies observed by JWST at $z\gtrsim10$. Using SED templates built from this IMF within a semi-analytic model on an N-body simulation, they find it enhances UV luminosity and its scatter versus SFR, and that the self-consistent model (including IMF-dependent dust) broadly reproduces the UV luminosity function at $z\sim10$, with best-fit dust optical depths at only 51% and 21% of fiducial values at $z=9.7$ and $13.04$.
ranked.why: Directly relevant to stellar population synthesis assumptions (IMF choice) that underpin SED/spectral fitting of high-z galaxies, showing how IMF and dust degeneracies interact.

ranked.title: Age dependence of the radial metallicity gradient in the Galactic disc with LAMOST and Gaia
ranked.abstract: We investigate the stellar radial metallicity ([Fe/H]) gradient--age relation (MGAR) of the Galactic disc using a solar-neighbourhood sample of 580\,037 F-, G-, and K-type (FGK) dwarf and turn-off stars from LAMOST DR7, Gaia Data Release3, and the corrected StarHorse age catalogue. The fiducial MGAR is non-monotonic, with relatively strong negative gradients at intermediate ages followed by substantial flattening towards older populations. The most negative gradient occurs at $6$--$8$ Gyr in the adopted 2-Gyr bins, although the $4$--$6$ Gyr slope is statistically similar, indicating a broad intermediate-age turnover rather than a sharply defined transition. The flattening persists within the low-$\alpha$ population, indicating that chemical-population mixing alone cannot explain the full-sample relation, and is also recovered under alternative guiding-radius definitions, radial fitting ranges, vertical-orbit selections, propagation of the reported random age uncertainties, and an alternative stellar-age scale. In contrast, controlling the age-dependent $T_{\rm eff}$--$\log g$ distribution substantially reduces the absolute gradient amplitudes and modifies the younger-age behaviour. A same-star comparison with APOGEE DR17 further shows that the broad age dependence of the controlled MGAR is recovered using an external [Fe/H] scale. We therefore identify the intermediate-to-old-age flattening as the most robust feature of the observed MGAR, whereas the precise location and depth of the intermediate-age minimum and the detailed younger-age morphology are less stable. These results indicate that stellar-parameter selection can contribute to the diversity of MGAR morphologies reported in previous studies.
ranked.reason: Milky Way disc metallicity-age relation from LAMOST/Gaia stellar spectra, adjacent (stellar not galaxy spectroscopy) but survey/stellar-population flavored.
ranked.summary: This study examines how the radial metallicity gradient of the Galactic disc depends on stellar age, using 580,037 FGK stars from LAMOST, Gaia, and StarHorse ages. The gradient is non-monotonic, steepest at 6-8 Gyr and flattening toward older populations, a pattern that persists across alternative definitions and is confirmed via an independent APOGEE comparison; however, controlling for the age-dependent $T_{eff}$-$\log g$ distribution substantially reduces the gradient amplitude, implicating stellar-parameter selection effects.
ranked.why: A methodological cautionary tale about how sample selection and derived stellar parameters can bias chemical-evolution inferences, a concern that transfers directly to spectroscopic pipeline choices for galaxy stellar populations.

ranked.title: Velocity-Window Dependence of the Broad H$\alpha$ Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots
ranked.abstract: Broad Balmer emission lines probe black hole masses and nuclear kinematics in high-redshift active galactic nuclei (AGNs). In JWST "little red dots" (LRDs), integrated broad-H$\alpha$ widths span a remarkably narrow range at fixed line luminosity, raising the question of whether this tightness persists once outer-wing emission is included. Holding each object and its broad-H$\alpha$ luminosity fixed, we measure the finite-window line dispersion $\sigma(V)$, the flux-weighted second-moment width within $\pm V$, from $V = 1500$ to $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in JWST/NIRSpec spectra and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Type-1 AGNs. Across 20 high signal-to-noise LRDs, the observed scatter in $\log_{10}\sigma(V)$ at fixed $L_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}$ rises from 0.036 to 0.084 dex between $V = 2500$ and $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, a paired increase of 0.048 dex with a 95% bootstrap interval of 0.026-0.064 dex, compared with 0.020 dex across 167 broader SDSS AGNs. Injecting synthetic profiles into the empirical noise of the same 20 spectra shows that single-Gaussian and core-plus-wing models both accommodate this rise, leaving intrinsic wing diversity, truncation, and wing noise unseparated. In the clearest dual-line spectrum, RUBIES-EGS-55604, H$\beta$ strengthens relative to H$\alpha$ from line center to wing under two spectral decompositions of the same grating spectrum. Alongside integrated widths in JWST, SDSS, and 334 Euclid DR1 AGNs, these results show that the observed tightness of the H$\alpha$ scaling depends on the velocities included in $\sigma(V)$, requiring mass and kinematic models to match both transition and velocity interval.
ranked.reason: AGN broad-line width study in LRDs using JWST/SDSS spectra, adjacent to galaxy spectroscopy but focused on BH masses not stellar populations.
ranked.summary: This paper tests whether the tight relation between broad H$\alpha$ width and luminosity in little red dots (LRDs) holds when wider velocity windows capturing line wings are included. Measuring finite-window dispersion $\sigma(V)$ across 20 high-S/N LRDs, the authors find scatter rises from 0.036 to 0.084 dex between $V=2500$ and $4500$ km/s (a 0.048 dex increase), much larger than in broader SDSS AGN samples, showing the apparent tightness depends on the velocity range used.
ranked.why: A methods-focused spectral-measurement result showing how line-fitting window choices can create or hide scaling-relation tightness, relevant to anyone extracting physical parameters from noisy emission-line spectra.

ranked.abstract: The Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) strong lens search presents ECLIPSE, the largest catalogue of strong gravitational lens candidates to date, with >15 000 systems identified across 1900 deg2 of sky. It was constructed using five neural networks applied to approximately 68 million galaxies, followed by citizen science and expert visual inspection. In this work, we compare how the independently developed networks use image information to identify their selection of strong lens candidates. The search combines convolutional neural networks and a vision transformer, using the same pool of data but with different image processing and training choices. We investigate why these networks find different systems and what that means for the completeness of our catalogue. We evaluate all networks on a 50 deg2 calibration set and their application to the full DR1 sample. We find that the networks score candidates very differently, and that combining them recovers over 500 lens candidates within our calibration set at an inspection budget of 2000 objects. On the full DR1 sample, we show that individual networks have distinct biases: some networks favour systems with a larger Einstein radius while others are more sensitive to compact configurations. We also investigate network preferences in terms of lens light profile, mass distribution geometry, photometric redshift, and magnitudes. These findings provide a detailed analysis of how neural network selection biases have shaped the Euclid DR1 ECLIPSE catalogue. The results inform how networks should be combined in future Euclid data releases and upcoming wide-field surveys such as LSST or Roman to maximise both completeness and diversity of the recovered lens population.

ranked.summary: This Euclid DR1 paper asks how five independently trained lens-finding networks (CNNs plus a vision transformer) differ in which strong lenses they select among ~68 million galaxies. They find the networks disagree substantially in scoring, each with distinct biases (e.g. Einstein radius, compactness), and combining them recovers over 500 additional lens candidates within a 2000-object inspection budget on a 50 deg2 calibration set.
ranked.why: A concrete, large-scale case study in ML model bias and ensembling for astronomical classification, useful as a template for thinking about selection effects in any deep-learning-based survey pipeline.

ranked.title: Chemical structure of the solar neighbourhood with DESI DR1
ranked.abstract: We analyse the chemical, spatial, and kinematic properties of stars in the solar neighbourhood using DESI Data Release 1 combined with Gaia astrometry. A high-quality FGK dwarf sample is separated into low-$\alpha$ and high-$\alpha$ populations using Gaussian mixture modelling in the [$\alpha$/Fe]--[Fe/H] plane. The low-$\alpha$ population is more metal rich, dominates near the Galactic mid-plane, and shows negative radial and vertical metallicity gradients. The high-$\alpha$ population is more metal poor, has a steeper vertical metallicity gradient, an approximately flat radial metallicity profile, and dynamically hotter kinematics. Despite these differences, the two chemically defined populations overlap substantially in velocity space. These results indicate distinct chemical enrichment histories for the low-$\alpha$ and high-$\alpha$ populations, while showing that chemical classification does not map uniquely onto present-day kinematic components. The observed chemo-dynamical structure is consistent with the combined effects of chemical enrichment, radial redistribution, and secular dynamical evolution in shaping the Galactic disc.

ranked.summary: Using DESI DR1 combined with Gaia astrometry, this paper characterizes the chemo-dynamical structure of solar-neighbourhood FGK dwarfs, separating low- and high-$\alpha$ populations via Gaussian mixture modelling in the [$\alpha$/Fe]-[Fe/H] plane. The low-$\alpha$ population is more metal-rich with negative radial/vertical gradients, while the high-$\alpha$ population is more metal-poor with a steeper vertical gradient and flat radial profile, yet the two populations overlap substantially in velocity space, showing chemistry does not map uniquely onto kinematics.
ranked.why: A direct demonstration of DESI's capability for large-scale chemical population studies and of the limits of simple chemo-kinematic classification schemes, relevant background for any DESI-based stellar population work.

ranked.title: Continuum Pumping Revises Metallicity in the Orion Nebula
ranked.abstract: The enrichment of heavy elements in the interstellar medium is central to understanding galaxy evolution. Oxygen, the most abundant element after H and He, provides the principal tracer of gas-phase metallicity, typically measured using nebular emission lines in star-forming regions. However, a long-standing issue-the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF)-produces a $\sim 0.25$ dex offset between metallicities derived from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs). We present deep spectroscopic observations of the Orion Nebula (M42), and use them to assess the contribution of the often neglected continuum pumping process. We find that the continuum pumping effect is at least a factor of two stronger than previously expected. After accounting for the flux contribution from continuum pumping, the RL metallicity is consistent with the CEL metallicity, thus explaining the bulk of the ADF. Reassessing O/H measurements in five literature star-forming regions using the same method, we similarly find a systematic reduction of RL-based metallicities. These results indicate that RL metallicities, which have previously been considered more reliable than CELs, are subject to potentially large bias from continuum pumping. This study provides a foundation to correct this bias and establish accurate element abundance scales throughout cosmic time.
ranked.reason: Nebular metallicity measurement systematics in Orion, spectroscopy-adjacent but HII region abundance physics not galaxy stellar populations.
ranked.summary: This paper investigates the long-standing abundance discrepancy factor (ADF, ~0.25 dex) between recombination-line (RL) and collisionally-excited-line (CEL) metallicities in the Orion Nebula, testing whether the often-neglected continuum pumping process contributes. Deep spectroscopy shows continuum pumping is at least twice as strong as previously assumed, and once corrected for, RL and CEL metallicities become consistent, explaining the bulk of the ADF; the effect is confirmed in five other literature star-forming regions.
ranked.why: Resolves a fundamental systematic in gas-phase metallicity measurement that underlies abundance scales used throughout galaxy chemical-evolution and stellar-population studies.

ranked.title: Joint Flow-Matching Posteriors for Overlapping LISA Galactic Binaries
ranked.abstract: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe millions of galactic binaries (GBs) at once, thousands of them resolvable, with signals that overlap in frequency. Separating them requires a global fit, a joint inference of all sources, which today takes Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers hours to days on a cluster and is repeated for each new stretch of data. We adapt recent advances in large-scale diffusion models, flow matching with a multimodal transformer, to learn the joint posterior once and then draw from it in a fraction of a second. We evaluate our approach on a realistic simulator, with full instrument response and noise, priors fitted to a simulated Galactic catalogue, and sources sampled anywhere in the entire 0.1 to 16 mHz frequency band. We demonstrate that the approach is scalable to up to 15 653 sources fitted simultaneously, evaluating calibration and coverage w.r.t. the MCMC baseline. The results show that this approach could be realistically scaled to tackle the full global fit problem.
ranked.reason: Flow-matching generative model for LISA source inference — ML/SBI methodology that could transfer, but applied to GW not spectra.
ranked.summary: This paper tackles the computational bottleneck of disentangling millions of overlapping LISA galactic binary signals, which normally requires hours-to-days MCMC runs per data segment. The authors train a flow-matching model with a multimodal transformer to learn the joint posterior once, then sample in a fraction of a second, demonstrating scalability to 15,653 simultaneously fit sources with calibration comparable to the MCMC baseline.
ranked.why: A strong example of amortized simulation-based inference replacing expensive MCMC for high-dimensional joint posteriors, a technique directly transferable to fast spectral parameter inference.

ranked.title: Multiphase Gas in the Ram-Pressure-Stripped Elliptical Galaxy NGC 1404
ranked.abstract: Galaxy groups and low-mass galaxy clusters are major sites of environment-driven galaxy evolution. NGC 1404 is an X-ray-bright early-type galaxy traveling through the intracluster medium of the nearby low-mass Fornax Cluster, and it hosts off-center warm ionized gas. With minimal ongoing stellar feedback and negligible active galactic nucleus feedback, NGC 1404 provides an ideal laboratory for constraining the impact of environmental processes on the thermodynamics of the interstellar medium. We analyzed VLT/MUSE, 506 ks Chandra ACIS, and 119 ks XMM-Newton RGS observations to quantify gas motions in both the hot and warm phases of NGC 1404. We probed the kinematics of the warm gas by deriving the velocity structure function (VSF) from MUSE H$\alpha$ integral-field spectroscopy. To measure the kinematics of the hot gas, we derived the power spectrum of X-ray surface brightness fluctuations from the Chandra data, and independently constrained galaxy-scale hot gas motions by measuring Fe XVII resonant scattering and turbulent line broadening with RGS. Our RGS spectral analysis gives a three-dimensional Mach number of $0.48^{+0.22}_{-0.14}$, consistent with the power-spectrum results from Chandra for the same extraction region, and corresponding to a turbulent-to-thermal energy density ratio of $\sim0.13$. The warm-gas VSF follows the expectation for Kolmogorov turbulence and is broadly consistent with the hot-gas kinematics. The off-center warm gas in NGC 1404 may have formed through radiative cooling of the hot interstellar medium, triggered by the uplift of low-entropy hot gas during ram pressure stripping. Our study suggests that ram pressure stripping can drive substantial gas motions and reshape the thermodynamic state of the interstellar medium of cluster member galaxies.
ranked.reason: Multiphase gas kinematics in a stripped elliptical via MUSE/X-ray, galaxy evolution environment study but not stellar populations or ML-driven spectroscopy.
ranked.summary: This paper studies gas kinematics in NGC 1404, a ram-pressure-stripped elliptical galaxy in the Fornax Cluster, combining VLT/MUSE, Chandra, and XMM-Newton RGS data. The warm ionized gas velocity structure function follows Kolmogorov turbulence and is consistent with hot-gas turbulence measured via X-ray surface-brightness fluctuations and Fe XVII line broadening, with an inferred 3D Mach number of $0.48^{+0.22}_{-0.14}$ and a turbulent-to-thermal energy ratio of ~0.13.
ranked.why: A detailed multiphase ISM/environmental case study; mostly tangential to stellar populations but relevant if interested in how environment reshapes gas available for star formation.

ranked.title: Quasi-hostless LRDs with intrinsically red, faint UV continua
ranked.abstract: High-redshift objects characterised by very weak UV relative to their strong, red rest-optical continua, with broad Balmer lines, appear to represent little red dots (LRDs) in their purest form: sources dominated by emission from their central engine (CE), sometimes dubbed black hole stars (BH*s). Previous work has selected BH*-dominated objects, where a BH* template dominates the rest-optical emission; this remains agnostic to the rest-UV. We therefore select low FUV-to-optical continuum ratio ($L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}<0.03$) objects resembling MoM-BH* and The Cliff, from a spectroscopic sample of 132 LRDs at $2\lesssim z\lesssim9$. This identifies three LRDs that we newly classify as BH*-like objects, more than doubling the existing sample: two at $z>6$ and one at $z\sim3$. The UV slope reddens as the NUV- ($L_{\rm 3500}$) and FUV-to-optical ratios fall, with $\beta_{\rm UV}$ rising from $-1.8$ at $L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}\sim 0.5$ to $-0.5$ at $L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}<0.03$, beyond values typically seen at these redshifts. As the UV-to-optical ratio weakens, gas-enshrouded BH emission appears to dominate, leading to the quasi-hostless regime: a weak, red UV continuum emerges alongside extreme Balmer decrements and weak forbidden line emission. This reddening could be reproduced by a simple model of a blackbody and hydrogen nebular emission leaking through a high column density screen of neutral hydrogen in the $n=2$ level ($N_{\rm H,\,n=2}\approx10^{17}\,{\rm cm^{-2}}$), combined with a relatively weak host galaxy, although alternative CE scenarios may also reproduce this reddening. The host galaxy's growing FUV contribution in this model results in a testable UV morphological evolution with wavelength. This work identifies a family of quasi-hostless LRDs that share a common, intrinsically red, rest-UV continuum originating from their central engine.
ranked.reason: LRD/AGN continuum study, not spectroscopy of stellar populations or ML methods central to the researcher's interests.
ranked.summary: This paper identifies a new subclass of little red dots (LRDs) whose UV continuum is so weak and red that the host galaxy appears nearly absent, selecting objects with $L_{1500}/L_{5100}<0.03$ from 132 spectroscopic LRDs and finding three new examples that more than double the known sample. The reddening trend ($\beta_{UV}$ rising from $-1.8$ to $-0.5$) is reproduced by a blackbody-plus-nebular-emission model leaking through a neutral hydrogen screen with column density $N_{H,n=2}\approx10^{17}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$.
ranked.why: Illustrates how extreme spectral decomposition can isolate AGN central-engine emission from stellar populations, relevant to full-spectrum fitting degeneracies in obscured high-z sources.

ranked.title: Unresolved binaries from Gaia XP to SPHEREx
ranked.abstract: Unresolved companions alter the luminosity and spectra of a star, but a colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) reveals them only when the system is over-luminous, and a Gaia photocentre orbit constrains only a combination of the mass and flux ratios. We fit the absolute Gaia BP/RP (XP) and SPHEREx spectra (XPS) of about 71,000 low-mass stars in the Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars with the J-CaPS XPS emulator, which predicts single-star and coeval-binary spectra on an absolute flux scale. First, more than half of known binaries lie within the main-sequence (MS) band of the CMD, because the companion is faint or lifts a metal-poor primary onto the single-star ridge. XPS recovers 86 per cent of the binaries that a CMD cut finds and 44 per cent of those it misses. Second, a small photocentre motion can come from a faint companion or a luminous one of nearly equal mass. XPS distinguishes them and recovers the mass ratios of double-lined binaries. Among substellar candidates with radial-velocity follow-up, it ranks all 11 binaries above all 16 confirmed brown-dwarf or planet hosts. The public package spbin provides this check before follow-up. Third, where XPS detects no companion light, we place an upper limit on the light of an MS companion. Among Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits with clean spectral fits, 2841 require more companion mass than XPS allows for a single MS star. Within 200 pc, their companion masses cluster at those of typical white dwarfs, and nearly circular orbits support this interpretation. Of 24 companions that joint radial-velocity and astrometric orbits show to be faint, XPS recovers 22, compared with 14 selected by the absence of a colour excess. Applied to forthcoming Gaia DR4 orbital solutions, XPS can help distinguish luminous binaries from substellar companions and identify candidate compact companions whose dynamical masses exceed the limits allowed by their light.
ranked.reason: Spectral emulator for detecting unresolved stellar binaries from Gaia/SPHEREx, data-driven spectral method but on Milky Way stars not galaxies.
ranked.summary: This paper asks how to detect unresolved stellar binaries that evade standard colour-magnitude diagram and Gaia photocentre-orbit methods. By fitting absolute Gaia XP and SPHEREx spectra of ~71,000 low-mass stars with a binary-spectrum emulator (J-CaPS), they recover 86% of CMD-identified binaries plus 44% of those CMD missed, and identify 2,841 Gaia DR3 astrometric systems requiring companion masses exceeding what a single main-sequence star could supply, consistent with white dwarf companions.
ranked.why: A nice example of a spectral emulator used for population-level inference and anomaly/companion detection, methodologically relevant to full-spectrum fitting and emulator-based inference approaches.

ranked.title: A Cross-Domain Simulator and Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Global 21-cm Inference
ranked.abstract: End-to-end uncertainty propagation in scientific inference often requires repeated evaluation of coupled simulators spanning multiple physical domains, often at prohibitive computational cost. Global 21-cm cosmology is an extreme example: a millikelvin cosmological signal must be separated from radio foregrounds and instrumental effects four orders of magnitude larger, making inference acutely sensitive to model misspecification. Reliable recovery is therefore contingent on an exceptionally accurate model that jointly propagates uncertainty through the complete observational chain. We present a differentiable, GPU-accelerated hybrid forward model combining neural emulation of the cosmological signal, a physics-informed multi-resolution parameterisation of the galactic foregrounds, and a linear surrogate model of the antenna. This unifies simulators spanning astrophysics and computational electromagnetics while reducing evaluation time by a factor of $7.2\times10^{7}$. Using GPU-accelerated Nested Slice Sampling, we benchmark the framework across 100 unseen signal realisations and find that 94 injected profiles lie entirely within their corresponding 95% credible bands. Together, the simulator and reference Nested Slice Sampling results provide a demanding benchmark of posterior calibration, mode coverage, and evidence accuracy across next-generation stochastic samplers, simulation-based inference, and variational inference frameworks.
ranked.reason: Uncertainty quantification benchmark for 21-cm cosmology inference, SBI/UQ methodology of secondary interest but applied to cosmology not spectra.
ranked.summary: This paper addresses uncertainty quantification for global 21-cm cosmology, where a faint signal must be separated from foregrounds four orders of magnitude brighter. The authors build a differentiable, GPU-accelerated hybrid forward model combining neural emulation, physics-informed foreground parameterisation, and an antenna surrogate, speeding up evaluation by a factor of $7.2\times10^7$, and show 94 of 100 injected test signals fall within their 95% credible bands using GPU-accelerated nested slice sampling.
ranked.why: A template for building fast differentiable emulators with calibrated uncertainty for a severely degenerate inference problem, a pattern directly reusable for spectral emulators and SED fitting.

ranked.title: Interpretable morphology-based marked statistics
ranked.abstract: The shapes and environments of cosmic structures carry cosmological information beyond the matter power spectrum. Recovering this information while retaining a physical understanding is a central challenge for cosmological inference. We construct an interpretable, rotation-equivariant neural marking scheme that reweights the matter field, combining learned density responses with explicit measures of local morphology. This approach enables direct inspection of the learned transformations, while retaining the advantages of a two-point function analysis. We employ a contrastive learning framework to align the marked summaries with the respective cosmological parameters. In real-space matter simulations, the learned marked spectra recover information beyond the ordinary power spectrum, tightening marginalized Fisher constraints on $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_m$ by factors of $1.7\times$ and $1.5\times$ relative to the power spectrum plus bispectrum at $k_{\mathrm{max}}=0.3\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Without retraining, our mark also improves a neutrino-mass forecast by a factor of $1.5\times$ relative to the power spectrum at the same scale cut. Across the cosmological prior, our marking scheme also improve the prediction errors in both parameters by $1.3\times$ over the best tested classical mark at $k_{\mathrm{max}}=0.2\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. A qualitative comparison with neural forecasts motivates the possibility that these different compressions approach a common information level. Neural marked statistics thus offer a route to extracting non-Gaussian information from cosmological surveys, combining interpretable, physically motivated transformations with the practical advantages of two-point estimators.
ranked.reason: Interpretable neural marked statistics for cosmological structure, ML methodology but applied to large-scale structure not galaxy spectra.
ranked.summary: This paper asks how to extract non-Gaussian cosmological information from the morphology of large-scale structure while keeping the method interpretable. They build a rotation-equivariant neural marking scheme trained with contrastive learning to align marked density summaries with cosmological parameters, tightening Fisher constraints on $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_m$ by factors of 1.7x and 1.5x relative to power spectrum plus bispectrum at $k_{max}=0.3\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$.
ranked.why: A concrete, well-benchmarked use of contrastive learning for interpretable physical summary statistics, a methodology transferable to representation learning on galaxy spectra.

ranked.title: Revisiting Evidence of Temperature Fluctuations in H II Regions. I. Interionic temperature differences
ranked.abstract: The oxygen abundance of H II regions is a fundamental tracer of chemical enrichment and gas cycling and is now routinely measured across a broad range of cosmic time. A persistent complication is the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF): the O$^{++}$/H$^+$ abundance inferred from optical recombination lines (RLs) is systematically higher than that inferred from collisionally excited lines (CELs). Small-scale temperature fluctuations within the O$^{++}$-emitting gas are among the most widely discussed explanations for this discrepancy. However, the recent identification of a substantial continuum-pumping contribution to the O II spectrum of M42 motivates a renewed assessment of which observations uniquely favor a temperature-based interpretation and which are also compatible with other mechanisms. In this first paper of a series, I examine the relation between the inferred temperature-fluctuation parameter, $t^2$, and interionic temperature differences, focusing on $\Delta T_e=T_e([OIII])-T_e([NII])$. Photoionization calculations show that ionization stratification naturally produces systematic temperature differences between the low- and high-ionization zones. Meanwhile, the conversion from an ADF to $t^2$ is strongly temperature dependent because CEL emissivities are nonlinear functions of electron temperature. I show that these two effects can account for much of the observed $t^2$-$\Delta T_e$ relation without requiring the interionic temperature difference itself to trace fluctuations within the O$^{++}$ zone. This result does not exclude temperature fluctuations in H II regions. Instead, it indicates that interionic temperature differences should be interpreted with care and, on their own, provide limited discrimination among proposed origins of the ADF.
ranked.reason: HII region temperature fluctuation theory paper, tangential to galaxy spectroscopy interests.
ranked.summary: This paper re-examines whether interionic temperature differences ($\Delta T_e = T_e([OIII]) - T_e([NII])$) in HII regions genuinely support the temperature-fluctuation explanation for the abundance discrepancy factor, motivated by the new continuum-pumping result in M42. Photoionization modeling shows ionization stratification alone can reproduce much of the observed $t^2$-$\Delta T_e$ relation, because CEL emissivities depend nonlinearly on temperature, meaning the data do not uniquely require fluctuations within the O++ zone.
ranked.why: A companion theoretical paper refining the physical systematics behind gas-phase metallicity measurements, useful context for interpreting abundance-discrepancy-affected spectra.

ranked.title: Resolved internal dynamics of a globular cluster candidate in a cosmological simulation at cosmic dawn
ranked.abstract: Globular clusters (GCs) are among the oldest and densest stellar systems in the Universe. Their compact sizes and old ages imply they must have assembled rapidly in the early Universe, yet the detailed physical mechanisms responsible for their formation remain uncertain. Although several scenarios have been proposed, cosmological simulations have so far been unable to resolve their detailed formation and internal dynamical structure at birth. Using a cosmological simulation that uniquely combines sub-parsec resolution with the formation of individual star particles, we follow the gravitational collapse and assembly of a compact stellar system with GC-progenitor mass and size, while directly resolving its internal dynamics and tracing the build-up of its angular momentum. The system assembles most of its stellar mass within 3 Myr, at $z\simeq10.5$, it rapidly becomes gas-poor, star-dominated, and develops ordered internal rotation acquired largely through the hierarchical assembly of distinct stellar subsystems. It forms as a satellite of a larger stellar complex within the virial radius of the $M_{\rm vir}\simeq1.73\times10^8\,M_\odot$ dark-matter halo hosting it. Its density, size and mass overlap with those of compact stellar systems recently observed by JWST at high redshift. These results indicate that GC progenitors can have well-defined internal kinematic structures already after their formation.
ranked.reason: Globular cluster formation in cosmological simulation, unrelated to galaxy spectroscopy or stellar population inference.
ranked.summary: This paper asks how globular clusters form and develop internal dynamics at cosmic dawn, using a cosmological simulation with sub-parsec resolution and individual star particle formation. A GC-progenitor system assembles most of its stellar mass within 3 Myr at $z\simeq10.5$ inside a $M_{vir}\simeq1.73\times10^8\,M_\odot$ halo, rapidly becoming gas-poor and developing ordered internal rotation through hierarchical assembly of stellar subsystems.
ranked.why: Mostly tangential to spectroscopy/stellar populations work, but relevant if tracking JWST-observed compact high-z stellar systems as potential GC progenitors.

ranked.title: Dynamical calibration of a metallicity-dependent stellar mass--luminosity relation from Gaia wide binaries
ranked.abstract: The mass of a main-sequence star is usually estimated from its luminosity through a mass--luminosity relation (MLR). This relation depends on metallicity, and its empirical calibration relies on few stars with measured masses. We calibrate the MLR of single main-sequence stars in the Gaia $G$ band as a function of metallicity with $10\,559$ wide binaries. The projected relative speed and separation of a wide binary constrain its total mass statistically. We describe the stellar mass as a monotone function of absolute magnitude and metallicity and fit this function to all pairs. The metallicities come from Gaia low-resolution (XP) spectra and are calibrated by requiring that both stars of a pair have the same metallicity. The likelihood includes the measurement noise, the selection of the sample and pairs with an undetected close companion. The data constrain the MLR over $3.7\lesssim M_{\mathrm{G}} \lesssim11.8$\,mag and $-0.5\lesssim\ \mathrm{[M/H]} \lesssim0.4$, with a median statistical uncertainty of $2.5\%$ in mass. Tests of the model assumptions indicate an additional systematic uncertainty of up to $5\%$. At solar metallicity the MLR agrees with the PARSEC models to within $5\%$. At the faint end, the MIST, BaSTI, Dartmouth and BHAC15 models predict masses 8 to $22\%$ below our MLR. Published masses from orbits, eclipsing binaries and asteroseismology lie within about $10\%$ of our MLR for $M_{\mathrm{G}}<10.5$ mag. For fainter stars they are about $17\%$ lower. The origin of the difference at the faint end is not yet understood. Because a shift of $0.1$ dex in metallicity changes the mass by up to $5\%$, MLRs should be compared on a common metallicity scale.
ranked.reason: Mass-luminosity relation calibration from Gaia wide binaries, stellar astrophysics but not galaxy spectroscopy/stellar populations.

ranked.title: The JWST Resolved Stellar Populations Early Release Science Program. X. Cross-Observatory Proper Motion Measurements with HST and JWST
ranked.abstract: We present the first absolute systemic proper motion (PM) of a galaxy measured by combining Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and JWST imaging. The PM of WLM, an isolated dwarf galaxy at $\sim$1 Mpc, is measured against background galaxies with Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) F814W imaging from 2015 and 2024 and NIRCam imaging from 2022 and 2024. The two ACS epochs give a systemic PM of $(\mu_{\alpha}^*, \mu_{\delta}) = (+0.087 \pm 0.019, -0.079 \pm 0.017)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 145 galaxies over 8.93 years, which agrees with previous Gaia-based PMs to within 0.4$\sigma$ and is the most precise PM of WLM. For the HST-to-JWST PMs, we fit each NIRCam detector separately, match the point-spread functions with empirically derived convolution kernels, and correct biases with injected galaxies. With an F090W second epoch, the PM is $(+0.081 \pm 0.045, -0.113 \pm 0.046)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 43 galaxies over 7.02 years, which, like the F150W PM, agrees with HST-to-HST over the same area to within 1$\sigma$, while F200W differs by $\sim$2$\sigma$. The long-wavelength F250M and F430M PMs are consistent to within 1$\sigma$, though less precise. Fewer galaxies can be used at wavelengths farther from F814W. A cross-observatory systematic of $\sim$0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ cannot be ruled out over 7 years. At equal baselines, an F090W second epoch is at least as precise as our second ACS epoch over the same area. We recommend the NIRCam filter closest in wavelength to the first-epoch filter, though the long-wavelength filters show promise for closer targets or longer baselines.
ranked.reason: HST/JWST proper motion astrometry of a dwarf galaxy, unrelated to spectroscopy or population synthesis.

ranked.title: Identifying Distant and Highly Reddened Star Clusters: 486 Open Clusters and Candidates in the Dusty Galactic Disk
ranked.abstract: The Gaia mission has transformed the census of Galactic star clusters. Most discoveries were based on Gaia DR2 and EDR3, and the rate of new large cluster catalogues has declined since 2023. The distant and dusty part of the disk is still poorly sampled because optical data are strongly affected by extinction. We search for star clusters in the Galactic disk using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, together with 2MASS near-infrared photometry. We scan trial cluster centers in Galactic position, proper motion, and parallax space, assign a Bayesian membership probability to each star, construct a relative density map, and use DBSCAN solely to separate neighboring peaks. We identify 486 clusters and candidates with astrometric quality comparable to that of previously reported clusters. Of these, 450 have no literature counterpart, while 36 are known clusters that were not recovered in earlier Gaia cluster searches. The median distance is 6.9 kpc, and 39% of the objects lie beyond 8 kpc. The median extinction is Av = 5.10 mag, and 16% of the objects have Av > 8mag. The new objects fill a sparsely sampled region of the distance--extinction plane. Their distribution reveals the north--south displacement of the Galactic warp, and high-latitude objects are on average farther, older, and less extincted. Gaia DR3 still offers room for distant, dust-obscured clusters, and this sample provides a baseline for Gaia DR4. All cluster parameters, member star information, spatial distribution maps, and color-magnitude diagrams can be downloaded from https://zenodo.org/records/24431850.
ranked.reason: Open cluster discovery via Gaia astrometry, no spectroscopy or galaxy evolution relevance.

ranked.title: Probabilistic Inversion of Strong Gravitational Lenses with Flow Matching Priors
ranked.abstract: Strong gravitational lensing reveals important information about the universe, but reconstructing the source image and lens properties requires solving an ill-posed inverse imaging problem. Generative image models serve as powerful data-driven priors in Bayesian inverse problems. Diffusion models have been used widely, but they are computationally costly. Flow matching has emerged as a promising alternative to diffusion models, with easier training, efficient sampling, and better-quality data generation. In this work, we present Blind-FlowSGS, a principled blind posterior sampling method using flow matching priors, enabling efficient posterior sampling for non-blind and blind inversion of strong gravitational lenses. On simulated Euclid data, we demonstrate our method's improvement over diffusion-based methods in both efficacy and efficiency. Our method shows promising capabilities to accurately process strong lensing data from modern sky surveys at scale. Our code and data are available on our project page.
ranked.reason: Flow-matching posterior inference method applied to strong lensing, ML/SBI methodology tangential interest but applied to imaging not spectra.

ranked.title: py4radiation: a framework for generating heating/cooling functions and ion fractions from custom radiation fields for astrophysical simulations
ranked.abstract: Modelling multiphase gas in and around galaxies is key to understanding the baryon cycle in galaxy evolution. Modern simulation codes rely on heating/cooling functions and ion fractions to capture the thermodynamics and chemistry of such gases, but coupling all physical factors remains challenging. We present a new Python-based, parallelised package that acts as an integration framework, connecting well-established astrophysical codes and models to produce self-consistent heating/cooling functions and ion fractions from custom ionising UV/X-ray backgrounds. The package returns multi-dimensional tables that can be readily coupled to hydrodynamic and post-processing codes to study radiative processes and extract observables, as we demonstrate with static cloud simulations. Our simulation suite studies the thermodynamic history of a static circumgalactic cloud with smoothed edges subjected to meta-galactic and starburst heating. We find that the clouds experience damped pulsations regulated by strong cooling-driven inflows and heating-driven outflows that constantly overshoot pressure equilibrium. Meta-galactic heating is weak and produces a confined and dense cloud, while starburst heating is strong and sustains large clouds only a little smaller than those obtained with the standard $10^4\,\rm K$ cooling floor. Starburst radiative heating acts as a damping agent, thereby reducing mixing. py4radiation comes with extensive documentation and a sample catalogue of heating/cooling functions and ion tables for a selected set of input meta-galactic and starburst spectral energy distributions. The code is publicly available and can be easily expanded.
ranked.reason: Simulation framework for heating/cooling functions, methods paper unrelated to galaxy spectroscopy or stellar populations.

ranked.title: The system initial mass function of Orion OB1b from probabilistic Gaia DR3 memberships
ranked.abstract: [ABRIDGED] Context: Whether the initial mass function (IMF) varies with environment remains a central question in star formation. The multiple populations of Orion OB1b provide an ideal laboratory to test possible IMF variations. Aims: We aim to characterise the stellar populations of Orion OB1b by identifying its constituent groups, assigning membership probabilities to individual sources, and determining their IMFs. Methods: Using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, we identified stellar groups through clustering analysis and assigned membership probabilities with a probabilistic mixture model. Stellar masses were derived from extinction-corrected photometry using pre-main-sequence evolutionary models. Results: We identified eight kinematically distinct groups and a non-clustered population, deriving ages and IMFs spanning ${\sim}0.08$--$10\,M_\odot$ for six groups, all consistent with being gravitationally unbound. Each IMF was fitted with a lognormal distribution below $1M_\odot$ and a power law above. The high-mass regime is statistically indistinguishable across all groups, while four groups also exhibit consistent IMFs over the full mass range. The remaining two groups show differences that may reflect membership uncertainties rather than intrinsic IMF variations. The combined IMF is characterised by $m_c=0.27^{+0.02}_{-0.02},M_\odot$, $\sigma=0.45^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$, and $\Gamma=1.85^{+0.16}_{-0.14}$. The non-clustered population exhibits a broader and more uncertain IMF, although residual field contamination cannot be ruled out. Conclusions: Our results support previous evidence for the complex internal structure of OB1b. The IMF in OB1b appears broadly consistent across its kinematically distinct groups and compatible with other young populations in Orion.

ranked.title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
ranked.abstract: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. Eleven of the 13 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations, for seven- and nine-parameter solutions alike, and the dynamical companion masses agree with the photometric estimates where the photocenter conversion is well determined. Independently of the fits, 33 of the 43 plausible systems with a usable position angle (77%) have the acceleration directed within 45 degrees of the primary-companion axis, against 50% for a control sample: DR3's measured accelerations point in the directions of the cataloged companions.

ranked.title: Geneva seven-colour synthetic photometry from Gaia DR3 spectrophotometry
ranked.abstract: The well-established calibrations of astrophysical parameters derived from classical photometric systems (e.g. those of Johnson, Stromgren-Crawford, and Vilnius) are rarely applied at present. Instead, spectral energy distribution fitting techniques and the very broad Gaia photometric system are typically employed. However, these approaches have proven highly inaccurate for upper main-sequence stars. In this work, the Geneva seven-colour photometric system was synthesised from flux-calibrated low-resolution Gaia spectrophotometry (BP/RP spectra). The available ground-based observations have made it the most homogeneous dataset, offering a number of astrophysical calibrations and applications. The GaiaXPy Tool was used to synthesise the seven filters. The original Geneva U had to be exchanged with the SDSS u because it is found to be significantly blueward of the cut-off of the BP/RP spectra. The ground-based observations were used to correct for offsets and the known temperature dependence of the effective temperature in the ultraviolet region of the BP/RP spectra. The test using well-known effective temperature and metallicity calibrations on the synthetic photometry (with 21 080 stars) demonstrated the high accuracy of this approach. Further checks for possible correlations between the projected rotational velocity and binarity yielded negative results. As a direct application, the metallicity of 630 open clusters (and, thus, the radial Galactic metallicity gradient) was determined. Finally, we compiled a catalogue of 25 881 397 objects. This work demonstrates that alternatives exist to the widely used three-band Gaia photometric system. The Geneva seven-colour approach can help calibrate and analyse astrophysical parameters, especially those of upper main-sequence stars.

ranked.title: The FRB Population Revisited: Rate, Energy, Evolution, and Host-DM Constraints from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
ranked.abstract: We present a study that simultaneously fits for key fast radio burst (FRB) population properties using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog while calibrating for instrumental selection effects. Our inferred volumetric rate at $z=0$ is $1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\times 10^{5}\,{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ above an isotropic-equivalent energy of $10^{39}$ erg and below a scattering timescale of 30 ms at 600 MHz. The evolution of the FRB rate relative to the cosmic star formation rate remains statistically unconstrained. Assuming a Schechter function for the energy distribution, isotropic emission, and 1-GHz emission bandwidth, we find a characteristic maximum energy of $2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0} \times 10^{41}$ erg and a differential power-law index of $-1.41\,^{+0.27}_{-0.21}({\rm stat.})\,\pm\,0.35({\rm sys.})$. The host galaxy contribution to the observed dispersion measure (DM) is modeled as a log-normal distribution; assuming a total Galactic contribution of 80 $\text{pc cm}^{-3}$, we find a median host-galaxy DM contribution of $199^{+34}_{-36}\;\text{pc cm}^{-3}$ in the rest-frame. Finally, we find that the average FRB spectrum, described by a spectral index of $\alpha=-1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$, is inconsistent with being flat at the $\sim2\sigma$ level. We note an excess of high-S/N bursts at low DMs in the observed sample that is not predicted by the best-fit model. Testing alternative models does not alleviate this tension; future population studies may mitigate this limitation by incorporating robust fluence and redshift measurements.

ranked.title: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
ranked.abstract: Recent observations of supermassive black hole jets extending up to the typical sizes of cosmic web filaments challenge our current understanding. In particular, the overall jet size of J152932.16+601534.4 ("Porphyrion") reaches $\sim 7$ Mpc at redshift 0.896. Magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) models of relativistic jets have never been successfully applied to such extraordinary distances, requiring demanding jet-environment and flow stability conditions. By using state-of-the-art numerical simulations of 3D relativistic-MHD jets, we show that Porphyrion's observational properties can be successfully modelled in a realistic scenario, involving a jet kinetic power of $3.5 \times 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and an external medium of a low-density galaxy group. We find that the pair of jets expands to $\sim 9$ Mpc in about $20$ Myr, implying that the jet grows with relativistic speeds for most of its evolution. Comparing this case with other jets of similar power propagating in substantially denser cosmic structures, we find much slower outflows that can only reach a few Mpc, consistent with the bulk of the observed population of giant radio galaxies. Our results make a testable prediction, i.e. future detections of even larger-scale jets in upcoming surveys and database searches will be invaluable in studying the demographics and feedback of the poorly known population of powerful jets, particularly in under-dense regions of the cosmic web.

ranked.title: XRISM view of a featureless cluster Abell 1060: Revealing the advection of a diffuse radio source by ICM motions
ranked.abstract: Abell 1060 is a nearby, dynamically relaxed galaxy cluster hosting the extended radio structure Flying Fox (FF) near its center. We used high-resolution XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy to measure intracluster medium (ICM) motions and velocity dispersion. Spatially resolved analysis reveals a velocity gradient of approximately 100 km/s along FF and enhanced velocity dispersion near the brightest cluster galaxy NGC 3311, suggesting turbulence generated by galaxy-ICM interactions. These results and the compact extent of FF favor fossil plasma supplied by past activity of the brightest cluster galaxy and transported by ICM motions. We also tested whether the measured turbulence could generate or maintain the nonthermal components of FF. For a velocity dispersion of $96.7^{+23.9}_{-24.6}$ km/s and an assumed turbulence scale of 50 kpc, comparable to the Resolve field of view and approximately half the cluster core radius, the turbulent energy flux is approximately $3.49 \times 10^{-28}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. Although this flux may weakly reenergize pre-existing relativistic electrons, the acceleration timescale of approximately 2.5 Gyr exceeds the synchrotron and inverse Compton cooling timescale of approximately 210 Myr. The present turbulence is therefore insufficient to accelerate electrons to high energies. In situ turbulent reacceleration is unlikely to dominate the generation of FF, although it may help maintain fossil electrons supplied by past AGN activity. These results link ICM dynamics to the origin of nonthermal emission and support a time-evolutionary picture of particle acceleration in galaxy clusters.

ranked.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
ranked.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

ranked.title: Modelling of post-reconstruction galaxy clustering with a hybrid bias expansion
ranked.abstract: Density-field reconstruction sharpens the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature and recovers part of the cosmological information lost from two-point statistics through nonlinear evolution. Exploiting reconstructed clustering beyond BAO measurements requires modelling nonlinear evolution and galaxy formation physics. We extend the hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion to post-reconstruction galaxy clustering in configuration space and determine its range of validity. We apply a single reconstruction displacement to each Eulerian basis field of a second-order hybrid expansion, retaining the same bias parameters before and after reconstruction. We fit the correlation-function multipoles of subhalo abundance-matching mocks in real and redshift space, considering RecIso and RecSym, and use a Fisher analysis to forecast constraints on $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_{\rm m}$. The model reproduces the pre- and post-reconstruction multipoles for $r>35 h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ with a single set of Lagrangian bias parameters. For a $3 h^{-3}\mathrm{Gpc}^3$ volume at $z\simeq0$ with $\bar{n}=5\times10^{-4} h^3\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, post-reconstruction clustering (POST) alone tightens the marginalised constraint on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ by a factor of $\sim1.3$ relative to pre-reconstruction clustering (PRE), but slightly weakens that on $\sigma_8$ when the reconstruction bias is inferred from the observed clustering amplitude. Combining PRE and POST reduces both marginalised uncertainties by about one third and increases the figure of merit by a factor of $\sim2.2$, mainly by breaking degeneracies between bias and cosmology. Pre- and post-reconstruction clustering contain complementary cosmological information and can be modelled within the same hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion. The framework is well suited to emulation and future joint full-shape analyses of galaxy surveys.

ranked.title: The MeerKAT absorption line survey: Galactic OH absorption at 18 cm
ranked.abstract: We present a blind search for Galactic OH 18-cm absorption lines towards 19,130 radio sources brighter than 1mJy at 1.4GHz, using 390 pointings of the MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS). We apply an automated line search followed by Bayesian nested sampling to identify OH 1667MHz, 1665MHz and 1612MHz absorption features, using HI emission and absorption profiles as physically motivated priors. We identify 15 confident detections of OH 1667/1665 MHz absorption. The majority of detections are associated with a visual extinction ($A_{\rm V}$) excess and, within the same MALS pointings, with detected CO emission and a high incidence rate of HI absorption, consistent with OH tracing the H$_2$-bearing medium. We also identify 9 candidates of OH 1612MHz satellite line absorption, two of which coincide with OH main line detections and show integrated optical depth ratios well above the LTE expectation of 1:9. As in previous studies, $N(\rm OH)$ shows no dependence on $N$(HI). Accounting for the varying sensitivity across sight lines, we estimate the covering fraction of OH-bearing gas at $\log N(\rm OH) > 12$ to be $C = 0.051 \pm 0.008$, providing an independent and a more precise estimate than previous measurements of the diffuse molecular gas. We also find qualitative evidence for a decrease of the covering fraction with Galactic latitude. Stacking reveals a clear OH absorption signal that becomes increasingly prominent when sight lines are weighted by $A_{\rm V}$ excess, independently confirming the association of OH with diffuse molecular gas. Modeling of the physical conditions yields hydrogen number densities of 10-100 cm$^{-3}$, typical H$_2$ column densities $\log N(\rm H_2) > 21$, and UV-flux to number density ratios of 0.01-0.3 Mathis cm$^{3}$, typical of the CNM.

ranked.title: Preliminary evidence for a Universal Magnetic Field Configuration in Disk-Galaxy Halos with POSSUM
ranked.abstract: We use the POSSUM catalog with its high density of background RM sources (30-50 per square degree) to extend previous LOFAR work and investigate the sign of galactic halo magnetic fields. We are searching for the universal configuration that arises if halo magnetization originates from a central Cosmic Battery, and is subsequently transported outward by large-scale outflows. Our analysis considers 10 edge-on galaxies in the field of view of the POSSUM survey with angular sizes between 60 and 100. For each such galaxy we collect all available background RM sources in a circular region with a radius of 2? around it. We rescale all galaxy sizes and their associated background RM source distances to a common galaxy size of 100 and stack all these regions together. We divide the stacked configuration of RM sources into the four quadrants on either side of the stacked galaxy axis. The mean RM of background sources is computed in each quadrant, and we obtain a pattern of positive and negative mean RM values around the stacked galaxy. A consistent, systematic RM-gradient pattern emerges inside about 6 stacked galactic radii, as expected in Magnetic Disk-Winds with the axial magnetic field configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. The inferred large-scale axial electric current in the halo flows from the center outwards. Beyond 6 galactic radii we observe the reverse mean RM pattern, as expected in the axial Magnetic Black-Hole Jet configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. Our work confirms the prediction of the Cosmic Battery, and presents one of the very few known signatures of the magnetic field in the halo and the circumgalactic medium (CGM).

ranked.title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
ranked.abstract: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.

ranked.title: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
ranked.abstract: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $\gamma=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $\rho_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1\sigma$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $\rho_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$, respectively. The leading halo monopole in the first two metrics is degenerate with the central mass. At fixed dynamical mass, their leading radial profile correction produces retrograde precession. The $\gamma=5/2$ metric introduces an additional angular deficit contribution, which enhances the precession response and accounts for its smaller parameter limits.

ranked.title: A Tributary of Tucana III? The Sutlej Stellar Stream in DELVE DR3
ranked.abstract: We present the first analysis of the Sutlej stellar stream using deep DECam photometry from the third data release of the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey (DELVE DR3). Sutlej was discovered in Gaia DR3 as two parallel branches of old, metal-poor stars in projection near the SMC. Our DELVE DR3 sample reaches $\sim$2.5-3.5 mag below the main-sequence turnoff of Sutlej, and with a main-sequence matched filter built from an isochrone fit to Sutlej, we recover both previously identified branches, and find additional structure between them and at the periphery of the stream, occupying a region of $\sim$11$^\circ$ $\times$ 7$^\circ$ scattered at $\sim$23-33 kpc. We investigate this region by separating it into four segments that have Sutlej-like properties. The isochrone is also consistent with the nearby ultra-faint satellite Tucana III (Tuc III), and the two systems have similar distances and proper motions. $N$-body simulations of a Tuc III-like satellite show that, once the passage of a massive LMC is accounted for, Tuc III's preceding pericentric passage was deep enough to strip most of the progenitor. The encounter with the LMC then spreads the debris across the Sutlej field at the observed distances and proper motions, though the models do not recreate the observed discrete overdensities. We find that Sutlej is compatible with a Tuc III origin.

ranked.title: Interactions between the magnetised jets in the twin radio galaxy J104455+354055
ranked.abstract: Pairs of galaxies in which both objects host kiloparsec-scale radio jets are extremely rare. Such systems provide unique opportunity to study the formation of relativistic jets and their resistance to side-way collisions with each other prior to their eventual merger. We analyse the radio data for the twin radio galaxy J104455+354055 associated with a pair of distant elliptical galaxies (z=0.163). The radio jets of both sources avoid disruption/merging for the initial tens of kiloparsecs. We investigate the role of the magnetic fields in the propagation of these radio jets. We used VLA radio data at high frequencies in both compact and extended array configurations to obtain sensitive high-resolution polarimetric data and study the properties of the magnetic fields in all jets. Polarisation data suggest shearing of the magnetic fields at points where the jets bend. The orientation of the magnetic field parallel to jet axis helps confine the jet. Such field configuration in two adjacent jets seems to prevent them from merging. The strength of the magnetic field slightly increases in jet bends and the associated shearing enhances the ordered component of the magnetic field. The more diffuse radio plumes at the end of each jet have comparable strengths and energies of the magnetic field. The twin radio galaxy J104455+354055 provides a unique possibility to study the interplay of radio jets of two radio galaxies. The analysis of the properties of the magnetic fields observed along the radio jets suggests that the wiggles and bends of these jets, caused by the likely interactions of the host galaxies, could be also governed by the magnetic fields that may prevent them from merging. The derived strengths and energies of the magnetic field in different parts of the jets should allow us to improve the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of radio galaxies.

ranked.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
ranked.abstract: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $\gamma = 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $\delta\Phi_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.
